title: HCP — Common definitions
description: Common value shapes of the Human Context Protocol (HCP) 2.0-draft-3, shared by the hcp/* tasks. Written for this registry from the HCP 2.0-draft-3 specification text (CC BY 4.0, https://github.com/loyalagents/hcp-spec), with attribution, and checked against the shapes HCP publishes for the same draft; not copied from HCP's own schema files. Where this schema and the HCP text differ, the HCP text governs. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty, which an hcp/* party never writes empty. hcp/import applies neither to an export it takes.

Urn.description: An HCP identifier: a UUID in `urn:uuid:` form, of any UUID version (HCP 4.2), as HCP uses for entry, grant, directive and retrieval identifiers.

Uri.description: An absolute URI with no whitespace, as HCP writes every custom value at an extension point (HCP A.3).

Category.description: An HCP context category (HCP 4.5), the primary unit of access control: either a slug from HCP's category registry, such as `general_preferences` or `health_context`, or a custom category written as an absolute URI under a domain its definer controls. A custom category is not portable between providers without bilateral agreement (HCP 4.5). The pattern admits the slug or an absolute URI's outline only: it carries no `format: uri`, which would refuse every slug, so checking that a custom value is a well-formed absolute URI, as HCP's prose requires (HCP A.3), is the consumer's check.

PurposeCode.description: An HCP purpose code: an absolute URI naming the purpose for which context is requested or may be used (HCP 6.1.5.2).

Assurance.description: How a Context Asserter's identity was established (HCP 3.6). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

RelationshipType.description: How one entry relates to another (HCP 4.2.3). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

MinimizationReport.description: The minimization report a query or get-entry result carries (HCP 7.5). It MUST NOT carry the number of entries considered, the number available within scope, or any other measure of what was withheld (HCP 7.5); no schema can check that by name.

method.description: The relevance method that determined the final ordering (HCP 7.3): the method the provider declares as `minimization_method` in its discovery document (HCP 19.3), such as `lexical`, `semantic` or `llm`, or `none` for a get-entry result. The set of values is open.
